title: Total charge calculation
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be q = 2B₀S/R.

title: Piecewise current function
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must correctly give I=0 for 0≤t≤π/(3ω) and I=-6ωB₀S/(πR) for π/(3ω)<t≤2π/(3ω).

title: RMS current value
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be I_rms = 2√3 ω B₀S/(πR).

title: Δω from energy balance
description: Essential: The final answer for part (4) must be Δω = 6B₀²S²/(π k m l² R).

title: Applying Faraday's Law
description: Important: The solution must use Faraday's law (ε = -dΦ/dt) to relate the changing magnetic field to the induced EMF.

title: Using Ohm's Law
description: Important: The solution must apply Ohm's law (I = ε/R) to find the induced current from the EMF.

title: Charge via flux change
description: Important: For part (1), the charge must be derived from q = ΔΦ/R, integrating the current or using Faraday's law.

title: RMS from energy equivalence
description: Important: For part (3), the RMS current must be found by equating the energy dissipated over a full period to that of a constant RMS current.

title: Energy conservation setup
description: Important: For part (4), the solution must set up an energy balance: the kinetic energy loss of the frame (times efficiency k) equals the electrical energy dissipated in the loop.

title: Sign error in current
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the sign (negative) for the current in part (2) is missing or incorrect relative to the defined positive direction.

title: Misinterpreting time intervals
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the piecewise function in part (2) uses incorrect time boundaries (e.g., not recognizing the zero-current interval from the B_y vs. t graph).

title: Algebraic simplification error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the approximation (1-x)² ≈ 1-2x for small x is misapplied in the energy equation for part (4).
